'
Ali Khalil
(
Chagatai
and
Persian
: علی خلیل), also known as
Ali-Sultan
(
Chagatai
and
Persian
: علی سلطان), was the
khan
(r.1339-1342)
[
1
]
of the
Chagatai Khanate
. He was a descendant of
Qadan
, son of the second
Great Khan
Ögedei
.
'Ali attacked the
ordo (palace)
of
Yesun Temur
and usurped the throne. He was the first and last one who had restored the Ögedeid authority over the Chagatai Khanate since the reigns of
Kaidu
and his son Chapar. During his reign, Islam fully absorbed the Chagatai
Mongols
and 'Ali persecuted followers of other religions. He is the one who ordered the killing of six Franciscan friars at Almalik in 1339, as depicted in
The Martyrdom of the Franciscans
, by
Ambrogio Lorenzetti
.
[
2
]
The Martyrdom of the Franciscans
, painted by Ambrogio Lorenzetti in 1342, took place in
Almaliq
in 1339. The central ruler who ordered the killing was Ali Sultan.
